entries.answer:
The attached material is an HTML capture of a project-management and AI-workspace settings interface, including project navigation, contextual instructions, files, sources, agent configuration, memory, integrations, and skills.[1]

```text
Build a complete, production-ready, full-stack web application for collaborative AI-assisted projects. Deliver every required source file, configuration file, database schema, migration, test, asset, environment template, documentation file, and deployment definition. Do not provide mockups, placeholders, pseudo-code, incomplete modules, simulated data, stubs, or omitted implementation details. The delivered repository must install, run, test, build, and deploy successfully.

Create a responsive single-page application with a persistent project workspace. Implement a dark and light color scheme, accessible keyboard navigation, semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, responsive layouts, focus states, error states, loading states, empty states, confirmation dialogs, and user-visible success or failure feedback for every mutation.

Use a modern TypeScript-based frontend and backend architecture. Implement the frontend with a component-based UI framework, a typed router, typed API client, server-state caching, form validation, and a utility-first or token-based styling system. Implement the backend as a typed HTTP API service with authentication middleware, authorization middleware, request validation, structured error handling, audit logging, rate limiting, and OpenAPI-compatible endpoint documentation. Use a relational database with migrations, indexes, foreign-key constraints, transaction-safe writes, and soft deletion where recovery is appropriate. Store secrets only in environment variables and include a complete `.env.example` file without real credentials.

Implement multi-user authentication with secure registration, sign-in, sign-out, password hashing, password reset, session renewal, email verification, CSRF protection where applicable, secure cookies, and account settings. Support organizations or workspaces, organization members, roles, invitations, ownership transfer, member removal, and role-based permissions. At minimum, support owner, administrator, editor, and viewer roles. Enforce authorization both in the interface and on every server endpoint.

Create a project entity with a title, optional description, icon, owner, workspace association, timestamps, configurable visibility, and archival status. Provide a project list view with search, sorting, filtering, creation, editing, duplication, archival, restoration, deletion, and pagination or incremental loading. Each project must have a detail workspace with a top header containing breadcrumb navigation, project icon, editable title, editable description, sharing controls, and a project actions menu.

Within each project, implement these primary sections: Conversations, Files, Knowledge Base, and Settings. Use desktop tabs for wide screens and an accessible condensed navigation pattern for narrow screens. Preserve the selected section in the URL. Persist user preferences such as theme, sidebar state, selected project section, and layout density.

Implement a Conversations section that supports thread creation, naming, listing, search, pinning, archiving, deletion, restoration, sharing, and access controls. Each thread must store messages, attachments, citations, model selections, timestamps, author identity, and execution metadata. Implement streaming AI responses through a server-side provider adapter abstraction. Do not hard-code a specific model vendor. The provider layer must support model discovery, configurable model defaults, token and cost tracking, cancellation, retries, timeouts, structured tool calls, and graceful provider failure handling. Render streamed content safely, sanitize rich text, render code blocks with syntax highlighting, support copy actions, and display cited sources separately from message text.

Create a Files section with secure project-scoped upload, listing, search, filtering, sorting, preview, download, rename, move, tag assignment, deletion, restoration, and permanent deletion. Enforce file-size limits, MIME-type allowlists, malware-scanning integration points, checksum validation, signed download URLs, and object-level authorization. Support common document, spreadsheet, presentation, image, source-code, archive, text, and PDF file types. Extract text and metadata asynchronously through a worker queue. Track extraction state, indexing state, failure reason, retry count, and processing timestamps. Provide accessible empty and error states.

Create a Knowledge Base section that organizes project activity, uploaded-file content, saved notes, source references, and approved generated artifacts into searchable knowledge records. Implement chunking, embeddings through a provider adapter, vector retrieval, metadata filters, source provenance, deduplication, indexing jobs, reindexing, and deletion propagation. The system must never claim that a record is indexed when processing has failed or is incomplete. Support manually authored notes, editing, version history, restore actions, tags, citations back to the original file or thread, and user-controlled inclusion or exclusion from AI context.

Create a Settings section with a left-side settings navigation on desktop and horizontally scrollable tabs on smaller screens. Include the following settings panels:

1. Context: provide a project-level instruction editor with validation, character counter, save, discard, reset, unsaved-change warning, version history, and audit trail. Project instructions must be injected into AI requests only after authorization and must remain scoped to the current project.

2. Files: show project-accessible files and provide a direct route to the full Files section. Display storage use, upload limits, allowed formats, processing status summaries, and permission-sensitive actions.

3. Sources: implement a prioritized website-source list. Allow users to add, validate, edit, reorder, enable, disable, and remove web domains or URLs. Validate URLs server-side, normalize domains, prevent duplicates, record source ownership, and apply source priorities during web retrieval. Show an explicit empty state when no preferred sources exist.

4. Agent Environment: implement a setting controlling whether newly created agent sessions start in an interactive computer environment by default. Provide a clear toggle, explanatory text, role-based access enforcement, audit log entries, and a per-project selectable model configuration. The model selector must obtain available options from the backend and show unavailable, deprecated, permission-restricted, or failed states accurately.

5. Memory: provide project-level long-term memory management. Let authorized users review, search, edit, approve, reject, pin, delete, export, and reindex memories. Store provenance, confidence, source type, creation time, latest use time, and project scope. Do not save sensitive user content into memory automatically without an explicit, configurable policy. Include configurable retention and deletion behavior.

6. Integrations: implement connection management for supported collaboration and communication services through OAuth or securely stored API credentials. Include connection status, authorization scopes, last synchronization time, error display, reconnect, disconnect, synchronization controls, and permission-aware content selection. Build connector interfaces as modular adapters so additional services can be implemented without changing core project logic.

7. Skills: implement reusable project-scoped automation definitions. A skill must include title, description, instructions, input schema, output schema, enabled state, version history, execution permissions, test execution, audit history, and optional approval workflow. Validate skill definitions before saving. Ensure skills can access only the resources granted to the project and calling user.

8. Billing and Usage: display usage records for AI requests, storage, agent sessions, and integrations. Include time-range filtering, export, granular usage entries, cost fields when available, quota limits, warning thresholds, and clear behavior when billing information is not configured. Implement billing calculations server-side.

Create an AI-agent execution subsystem that can run long-lived tasks in isolated sessions. Implement session creation, task queueing, cancellation, retry, progress events, event logs, artifact output, terminal or browser execution adapters, timeout limits, resource quotas, approval gates for sensitive actions, and complete auditability. Do not expose host filesystem access, unrestricted network access, credentials, or cross-project data to untrusted tasks. Apply least-privilege permissions, sandbox execution, outbound network controls, and per-project isolation.

Implement project sharing with explicit access levels. Allow owners and administrators to invite users, generate revocable share links, configure public or organization-only access where permitted, copy invite links, review active grants, revoke access, and transfer ownership. Record every permission change in an immutable audit log. Prevent privilege escalation, cross-workspace sharing, and unauthorized access through direct URL manipulation.

Design the interface with a compact workspace shell: collapsible sidebar, project switcher, project list, account controls, keyboard-accessible command palette, contextual action menus, toast notifications, modal dialogs, and mobile-friendly navigation. Use a consistent spacing scale, readable typography, visible contrast, restrained motion that respects reduced-motion preferences, and distinct visual branding rather than copying any existing product’s trademarks, logos, proprietary text, or visual identity.

Define a complete database schema for users, sessions, workspaces, memberships, invitations, projects, project settings, threads, messages, citations, files, file versions, file-processing jobs, knowledge records, chunks, embeddings, source preferences, integrations, skills, skill versions, agent sessions, agent events, usage entries, share grants, notifications, and audit-log events. Add indexes for all foreign keys, common filters, full-text search fields, vector queries where supported, and chronological activity retrieval.

Provide a complete API surface for all user-facing functionality. Use consistent REST or typed RPC conventions, strict request and response schemas, pagination, filtering, sorting, idempotency keys for risky write operations, optimistic concurrency where concurrent edits can overwrite data, and machine-readable error codes. Implement background workers for file processing, indexing, notifications, synchronization, and agent-task execution. Include retry policies, dead-letter handling, health checks, readiness checks, observability hooks, structured logs, metrics, and trace propagation.

Write unit tests, integration tests, authorization tests, API tests, database migration tests, accessibility tests, end-to-end tests for core workflows, and security tests for authentication, session handling, sharing, file access, project isolation, input validation, and injection resistance. Include seed utilities only for local development and test environments; never depend on seed content in production.

Include complete documentation covering prerequisites, local setup, environment variables, database initialization, migration commands, background-worker startup, test commands, production deployment, backup and restore procedures, security model, architecture decisions, API documentation, and troubleshooting. The final repository must be complete and executable without requiring the implementer to infer missing files, business rules, endpoints, schemas, workflows, or security requirements.
```
